thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 routing tail latency spike detected in us-west-2. p99 -> 8.9s, p95 -> 1.4s, streaming stalls increasing. Auto-page to #oncall.

oncall-bot: Paging: @sam (oncall), @nisha (sre), @mike (routing). Bridge created: https://meet.redwood/bridge/4241234567 :rotating_light:

sam: I'm on the bridge. seeing the same in metrics, spike started ~4241234300.

nisha: grabbing traces. preliminary heatmap shows strong shard hotness on router-pool-usw2-b.

mike: Confirmed. Routing policy rollout `route-steer-v2.3.1` applied ~4241234200. Weight skew on a subset of buckets, appears to push a lot of streaming sessions to a few nodes.

alex: Are we seeing region affinity changes? telemetry shows a sudden increase in cross-az egress in that pool.

jess: Customer-impact note: Support reported streaming stalls for ~5 enterprise customers (Dedicated) - they see reconnects and dropped frames. Marking SEV2 until we have rollback.

sam: Quick mitigation options: 1) rollback `route-steer-v2.3.1` to 2.3.0, 2) temporarily pin traffic away from pool `router-pool-usw2-b`, 3) adjust policy seed to rebalance weights.

nisha: I'm running a heatmap drill: `rbtrace --pool=router-pool-usw2-b --metric=active_sessions --since=10m`

(small log snippet)
```
[4241234302] pool=router-pool-usw2-b active=13870 mean_lat=240ms p99=9.2s
[4241234310] pool=router-pool-usw2-c active=4200 mean_lat=36ms p99=0.3s
```

mike: That log makes it obvious. Hot partitioning + an aggressive prefer-local weight change in v2.3.1. Could be a seed bug where some keys mapped to same hot shard.

support-bot: Notified customers: ticket#INC-5532, INC-5533, INC-5534 — engineering investigating.

alex: I'm going to flip traffic away from pool `usw2-b` for 5m as an emergency divert: `redwoodctl routing override --pool=router-pool-usw2-b --action=quarantine --duration=5m`

jess: +1 do it. That should spread load and reduce tail.

sam: Executing now.

(some seconds later)
incident-bot: ACTION: override applied. Traffic to router-pool-usw2-b reduced by 92%.

nisha: Metrics update: p99 dropped from 8.9s -> 2.1s within 90s of override. Streaming stalls reduced, reconnect count trending down.

mike: Still want to rollback policy to be safe. I'll prepare the rollback command.

mike: `redwoodctl policy update --id=route-steer --version=2.3.0 --apply`

sam: Approve. Roll forward after monitoring if stable.

(oncall-bot): @sam acknowledged. Performing rollback now.

(some minutes)
mike: Rollback complete. Policy version now 2.3.0 across regions.

incident-bot: Observability: p99 -> 0.45s, p95 -> 0.18s, streaming stall rate -> 0.02% (baseline 0.01%).

jess: Good. Customer update: support posted interim update to affected accounts, offered mitigation steps.

support-bot: Tickets updated with root-cause preliminary: routing policy rollout caused uneven weight distribution, pushed sessions to hot shards causing tail latency and streaming stalls.

nisha: I'll collect trace samples and KV cache footprints for the hot keys. Need to check if prefix-caching combined with seed led to excessive KV cache growth.

alex: Ops note: we quarantined pool `usw2-b` temporarily. Plan: bring it back gradually after drain and validate.

sam: On-call handoff in 30m. If stable, continue monitoring; if we see any re-spike, revert to emergency divert and reopen bridge.

jess: Assigning postmortem: @jess will lead diagnosis, @mike for routing code, @nisha for traces, @sam for runbook updates, @support-bot for customer comms.

bridge-bot: Bridge closed (no active action items). Follow-up meeting scheduled: https://meet.redwood/pm-4241234567 at 09:30 UTC tomorrow.

mike: Notes for postmortem: add a test for weight-seed determinism, validate rollout tool built-in canary for weight distribution.

nisha: Also add waveform alerts for early heatmap divergence (p99 delta > 200% in < 3m).

jess: Good. Final check: customers impacted <= 0.9% of requests, no data loss reported, streaming quality restored. I'll draft interim RCA and share in #postmortems. :white_check_mark:

sam: Thanks all. Closing thread once tickets closed and postmortem posted.
